entry_assumptions: Circle definitions: centre, radius, chord, arc, sector, and segment.
Perpendicular from circle centre to chord bisects the chord.
Angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining circumference.
Angles in the same segment of a circle are equal.
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary (sum to 180 degrees).
Pythagorean theorem in Euclidean plane geometry.
inferential_jump: Progressing from foundational Euclidean chord bisection and subtended angle theorems to multi-stage Olympiad invariants: annulus area independence from individual radii, concyclicity of orthocenter altitude feet, Ptolemy's diagonal product identity, secant-tangent power invariants, and Euler's incenter-circumcenter distance relation.

hypotheses: Circles have real positive radii R > 0.
Points lie on well-defined circles or circular arcs.
Concentric circles share the identical centre O with R > r.
Secants and tangents adhere to standard Euclidean incidence axioms.
excluded_values: Collinear triads masquerading as circular arcs.
Negative length segments or non-Euclidean curvature.

representation.symbol: OM perp AB implies AM = MB = AB / 2
representation.word_meaning: Perpendicular bisection invariant: the perpendicular from centre O to chord AB bisects the chord, forming right triangle OMA with hypotenuse OA = R.
Angles in the same segment: chords AC and BD intersecting at E create equal inscribed angles subtending the common arc BC.
Intersecting Chords Theorem: product of segments of two intersecting chords inside a circle is invariant due to similar triangles (triangle PAC ~ triangle PDB).
Mamikon Annulus Invariant: chord AB of outer circle tangent to inner circle at T yields ring area depending solely on chord length AB, independent of individual radii.

representation.symbol: angle(HDC) = angle(HEC) = 90 deg implies CDHE cyclic
representation.word_meaning: Concyclic altitude feet: altitudes AD and BE in triangle ABC subtend supplementary right angles at D and E, proving CDHE cyclic with diameter CH.
Dual circle secant parallelism: cyclic quads ABFE in C_2 and ABCD in C_1 transfer supplementary angles across shared chord AB to force EF || DC.

representation.symbol: d_1 * d_2 = AC * BD = AB * CD + BC * DA
representation.word_meaning: Ptolemy's Theorem: for any cyclic quadrilateral, the product of the lengths of the diagonals equals the sum of the products of opposite sides.
Secant-Tangent Power of a Point: tangent PT from external point P and secant PAB satisfy PT squared equals the product of external segment PA and entire secant PB.
Euler's Incenter-Circumcenter Distance Formula: the distance d between circumcenter O and incenter I satisfies d^2 = R(R - 2r), establishing Euler's inequality R >= 2r.

cognitive_scaffolding.band_d1_anchors: Direct Pythagorean chord distance, angle subtended by chord equal to radius, diameter right angle.
cognitive_scaffolding.band_d2_bridges: Intersecting chord products, cyclic trapezoid symmetry, exterior angles of cyclic quadrilaterals, dual-chord distances.
cognitive_scaffolding.band_d3_leaps: Mamikon annulus invariant, orthocenter concyclicity, external secant half-difference, Van Schooten equilateral triangle invariant.
cognitive_scaffolding.band_d4_syntheses: Ptolemy theorem diagonal product, secant-tangent quadratic power equations, inradius-circumradius relations, Euler distance invariant.

pillar_1_axiomatic_metric.name: Euclidean Chord Metric & Perpendicular Invariants
pillar_1_axiomatic_metric.algebraic_nature: Quadratic Pythagorean relationship between distance, radius, and semi-chord.

pillar_2_angular_concyclicity.name: Subtended Arc & Inscribed Angle Concyclicity Invariants
foundational_theorems: Euclid III.22 (Opposite Angles of Cyclic Quad)
pillar_2_angular_concyclicity.algebraic_nature: Linear angular summation and 2:1 homothety between central and perimeter angles.

pillar_3_power_of_point.name: Projective Chord Products & Tangency Invariants
pillar_3_power_of_point.governing_equation: PA \cdot PB = PC \cdot PD = |OP^2 - R^2| = PT^2
pillar_3_power_of_point.algebraic_nature: Constant projective power invariant based on distance from point to circle centre.

pillar_4_advanced_quadrilateral.name: Cyclic Diagonal Products & Inversion Invariants
pillar_4_advanced_quadrilateral.governing_equation: AC \cdot BD = AB \cdot CD + BC \cdot DA \iff ABCD \text{ is cyclic}
pillar_4_advanced_quadrilateral.algebraic_nature: Quadratic product bilinear form characterizing cyclic points via triangle inequality on inverted images.

pillar_5_triangle_center_concyclicity.name: Triangle Center Loci & Extremal Distance Invariants
pillar_5_triangle_center_concyclicity.algebraic_nature: Bilinear radical relationship connecting inradius, circumradius, and center separation.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.naive_misconception: Treating perpendicular chord distance as linear difference d = R - L/2.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.mathematical_refutation: Perpendicular from centre forms a right triangle with hypotenuse R and base L/2; distance is strictly non-linear: d = \sqrt{R^2 - (L/2)^2}.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.governing_invariant: Pythagorean metric invariant in right triangle OMA.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.naive_misconception: Assuming opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral are equal, like a parallelogram.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.mathematical_refutation: Central angles of opposite arcs span 360 degrees, forcing their halves to sum strictly to 180 degrees (supplementary, not equal).

cognitive_conflict_matrix.naive_misconception: Writing Secant-Tangent power as PT^2 = PA * AB (multiplying external segment by internal chord).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.mathematical_refutation: AA similarity between triangle PTA and triangle PBT pairs side PA of smaller triangle with entire secant PB of larger triangle: PT^2 = PA * PB.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.naive_misconception: Believing annulus area requires knowing individual inner and outer radii R and r.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.mathematical_refutation: Area = \pi(R^2 - r^2). The right triangle at the point of tangency gives R^2 - r^2 = (L/2)^2 directly, making individual radii completely irrelevant.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.naive_misconception: Applying Ptolemy's formula d_1 * d_2 = ab + cd with adjacent side products.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.mathematical_refutation: Ptolemy's theorem strictly pairs OPPOSITE sides: d_1 * d_2 = ac + bd. Pairing adjacent sides yields an inequality.
